newsitem.title: USA: Sears Western Auto repositioning itself.
newsitem.headline: Sears Western Auto repositioning itself.

text.p: Western Auto Supply Co, a unit of Sears, Roebuck and Co, said Thursday it unveiled a 15-month multi-million dollar plan to reinvent itself.

Under the repositioning, the company will add up to 100 new Parts America stores and convert more than 240 company-owned Western Auto outlets into a parts-only format. Western Auto also will exit the Dallas, Texas, and Jacksonville, Florida, markets, closing 25 stores.
Western Auto said its effort would involve phasing out the automotive services portion in more than 240 company-owned stores. Stores in Puerto Rico will not be affected by the decision.
The 100 new Parts America stores are scheduled to come on line this year. The second phase of the alignment will include adding an estimated 350 new stores by 1999.
A company spokesman said Western Auto would spend about $100 million over three years on the initiative.
"This new focus enables us to strengthen our market position and provide associates with unprecedented opportunities for growth," Western Auto chairman Donald Shaffer said in a statement.
Western Auto operates and manages 339 Western Auto company-owned stores, 850 Western Auto associate stores and 288 Parts America Stores.
